{{family name hatnote|[[Deng (Chinese surname)|Deng (鄧)]]|lang=Chinese}}
'''Lee C. Teng''' ({{zh|t=鄧昌黎|p=Dèng Chāng–lí}}; 5 September 1926 – 24 June 2022) was a Chinese-born physicist known for his work with the [[Advanced Photon Source]] of the [[Argonne National Laboratory]]. He made numerous contributions to the field of [[accelerator physics]].

==Career==
Teng was born in [[Beijing]], [[China]], but his [[Ancestral home (China)|ancestral home]] was in [[Fuzhou]]. He graduated from the [[Catholic University of Peking]] (now [[Fu Jen University]]) in Beijing in 1946. Teng left his native China in 1947 to attend graduate school in physics at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>[http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/31530 "Lee Teng: a passion for the accelerator fast lane", Cern Courrier, Oct. 17, 2007]</ref>

After receiving his [[PhD]] in 1951, Lee worked at the [[University of Minnesota]], the [[Wichita State University]], [[Argonne National Laboratory]], and the [[Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] (Fermilab). He was the director of the Particle Accelerator Division at Argonne National Laboratory.

In 1983, Teng took a partial leave of absence from Fermilab to serve as the founding director of what is now the [[National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center]] (NSRRC) in Taiwan.

==Honors==
In 1956, on his first trip to Taiwan, he was awarded the Gold Medal of Achievement by the [[Ministry of Education (Taiwan)|Ministry of Education]].

In 1957, he was elected an APS fellow.<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=T&year=&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=11 September 2023 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>

He received the Distinguished Service Award from the American Immigrants Service League in 1962.

In 1966 he was elected to member (Academician) of [[Academia Sinica]].<ref name="as">{{cite news |title=Lee C. Teng |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=148 |access-date=11 September 2023 |publisher=Academia Sinica}}</ref>

He was conferred an honorary professor of the [[Beijing Normal University]] in 1970.

In 2007, the [[American Physical Society]] awarded Teng the Robert R. Wilson Prize for Achievement in the Physics of Particle Accelerators.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lee Teng Awarded the 2007 Robert R. Wilson Prize by the American Physical Society |url=https://www.aps.anl.gov/APS-News/2017/lee-teng-awarded-the-2007-robert-r-wilson-prize-by-the-american-physical-society |access-date=11 September 2023 |publisher=Argonne National Laboratory |date=January 7, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=2007 Robert R. Wilson Prize for Achievement in the Physics of Particle Accelerators Recipient |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Teng&first_nm=Lee&year=2007 |access-date=11 September 2023 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>

The Lee Teng Internship in Accelerator Science and Engineering<ref>[http://www.illinoisacceleratorinstitute.org/ Lee Teng Internship in Accelerator Science and Engineering]</ref> was created jointly by Argonne, Fermilab, and the US Particle Accelerator School in 2007, in his honor.

==Death==
Teng died on 24 June 2022, after a period in hospice care.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lee Teng Obituary |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/chicagotribune/name/lee-teng-obituary?id=35529090 |website=Legacy |access-date=29 July 2022}}</ref>
